business_scope.primary_industry_name: Global App Store Optimization and Multilingual Organic Search

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Code civil, Code de commerce; AML/CFT provisions in Code monétaire et financier)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L561-1 to L561-57 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier); Article L561-45 et seq. on beneficial owner declarations; Decree No. 2017-1094 of 12 September 2017; Articles L123-1 to L123-17 of the French Commercial Code; EU AMLD 4/5 obligations transposed.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of constitutional articles or incorporation certificate of the foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or official body in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized identification document (passport) of each identified beneficial owner, director and signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notarial authority in the country of residence of the individual

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax residence certificate of the ultimate beneficial owner or a banking reference letter from the account-holding institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Revenue authority or financial institution of the country concerned

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation by a sworn translator of all foreign company documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court-sworn translator (traducteur assermenté) recognized by French judicial authorities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of signature, then Apostille OR Consular Legalization where required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, legal representatives, and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, EU Council Sanctions Map, French asset-freezing measures (Tracfin 'gel des avoirs'), and domestic French files; enhanced customer due diligence where a PEP is identified; continuous negative news monitoring and risk re-scoring before incorporation and during first AML review cycle.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprise managed by INPI (procedures.inpi.fr), with RCS registration at the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; official registry rests with the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be written in Latin characters; words in French are preferred and any foreign word must be phonetically transliterable into French; the name must contain no purely numerical code and must be sufficiently distinct to avoid confusion with existing RNCS registrations and trademark databases (INPI national mark database).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name rejection notice is delivered via the Guichet unique portal with a motivated administrative explanation; the applicant may submit an administrative reconsideration to the INPI within 30 days of rejection; subsequent judicial appeal may be filed before the President of the Tribunal de Commerce (or Tribunal Judiciaire in civil matters) within 15 days of the administrative refusal; name reservations may be renewed for successive 30-day windows up to a maximum of three renewals.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only through a registered domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) formally contracted under Articles L123-11-1 et seq. of the French Commercial Code; the domiciliation provider must provide a physical French address, mail handling, and access to the premises; a purely remote or postal-only address without a valid domiciliation contract is not acceptable for RCS registration or banking under AML/CFT rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 12% annual probability for a low-risk digital agency under normal circumstances; the probability rises above 25% if the registered address is held by an unvetted domiciliation provider, if inconsistent UBO documentation appears, or if Tracfin or relevant control authorities launch a sectoral inspection campaign.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (SAS), L.210-1 to L.210-10 and R.210-1 et seq., as amended; Decree No. 2023-873 implementing the electronic Guichet Unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: INPI Guichet Unique and Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) of the Commercial Court (Tribunal de commerce)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Digital formation dossier of a Société par Actions Simplifiée comprising the signed statuts (articles of association), declaration of incorporation, capital deposit certificate, legal publication certificate and beneficial owner declaration filed through the Guichet Unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SAS has no legal minimum share capital; the capital is freely set in the articles. The entirety of the share capital must be subscribed. At least 50% of cash par value must be paid up at formation (balance within five years); in-kind contributions must be fully paid up upon filing. The paid-up funds must be deposited with a bank, notary or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations and evidenced by a capital deposit certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: THE UNDERSIGNED SHAREHOLDER, holding 1,000 shares comprising the entire share capital of EUR 1,000, formally resolves: (1) the full subscription and payment of the share capital is approved, and the capital deposit certificate is acknowledged; (2) the registered office is fixed at 12 Rue de la Paix, 75002 Paris, France; (3) Ms. Claire Dupont is appointed President of the SAS, with full authority to act as legal representative and to exercise all powers granted by law and the articles of association; (4) the President and the shareholder are jointly authorised to complete all incorporation filings, legal publications and RCS registration formalities. This resolution is effective as of the date of signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholder; optional notary (not required for cash-only SAS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the French-language articles of association (statuts) setting out the corporate form SAS, legal name, registered office, duration (not exceeding 99 years), share capital, corporate object (global app store optimization, SEO localization and growth marketing services), governance rules, powers of the President, share transfer restrictions and references to the applicable standards. Have the articles signed by the sole shareholder or, where applicable, by all co-founders; if in-kind contributions exceed EUR 75,000, appoint a contribution auditor (commissaire aux apports).
required_dossiers: Identity document of the shareholder and proposed President
Proof of residential address of the shareholder and President
Draft of the articles of association (statuts)
Declaration of non-conviction (bulletin n°3) for the President if relevant
Proof of in-kind contribution valuation report, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bylaws contain errors or unresolved reservations regarding the corporate object, amend the articles by shareholder decision and re-execute all signatures before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a French Bank Account and Blocked Deposit of the Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in France or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations for blocked account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a professional bank account in the name of the company in formation and deposit the full amount of the paid-up share capital (at least 50% of cash contributions; no paid-up capital requirement for the remainder at formation). Request the bank to issue a capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds) identifying the company, the amount deposited and the account holding institution. This certificate is indispensable for the subsequent registration application.
required_dossiers: Articles of association signed for the purpose of the bank
Identity documents and KYC information for the shareholder and authorized signatories
Statement of the corporate object and expected transactions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of bank refusal or delayed account opening, apply to the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations under Article R.227-1 Code de commerce for a deposit without a bank or, alternatively, submit a declaration of full payment into the hands of a notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Legal Formation Announcement (Annonce légale)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved legal gazette (journal d'annonces légales) located in the department of the registered office; or regional authorized online platform.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the mandatory legal notice in a newspaper authorised to publish legal announcements in the court district of the registered office. The notice must contain the legal form (SAS), corporate name, share capital amount, registered office, business purpose, duration, and the identity and powers of the President. After publication, obtain the certificate of publication (attestation de parution).
required_dossiers: Completed legal announcement data sheet
Articles of association (if requested by the gazette)
Proof of registered office physical address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication is rejected or the certificate is delayed, contact the legal gazette to correct the financial data and republish, and obtain an issuance date confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the Formation File to the Guichet Unique and RCS Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), with final registration by the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) before the Commercial Court.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the official single window (guichetunique.inpi.fr), complete the digital company creation declaration (previously the M0 form), attach the statutory dossier, designate the President, declare the beneficial owners (bénéficiaires effectifs), pay the official drafting fee, and transmit. INPI will route the file to the competent RCS registry. The company will be registered and assigned a SIREN/SIRET number and an RCS reference; the final extract Kbis will be made available online.
required_dossiers: Signed articles of association (original scanned copy)
Capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds)
Legal publication certificate (attestation de parution)
Proof of registered office (lease, domiciliation contract or property title)
Identity document and address of the President
Declaration naming the beneficial owner(s) (bénéficiaires effectifs)
Power of attorney if filed through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a refusal, an observation notice or a request for completion, connect to the Guichet Unique to lodge a corrective declaration within the prescribed period (generally 15 days) without reinstating the time limits; all omissions and inconsistencies must be resolved online and the INPI will send the corrected file to the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activation of Tax and Social Registrations and Publication of Update Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INSEE (assignment of the SIREN/SIRET identifier), Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (VAT registration) and the social protection care for the President.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the RCS registration, confirm the automatic communication of the SIREN/SIRET to the business tax authority. Obtain the French intra-Community VAT number via the DGFiP local service (Service des Impôts des Entreprises). File the initial 'notice of statutory amendments' with the RCS if the President's powers or data differ, and register with the social security URSSAF or appropriate caisse if the President receives remuneration or is assimilated to a salaried status.
required_dossiers: Extract of the company's registration (extrait Kbis)
Identity and social security number of the President
Declaration of any remuneration or corporate benefits
Bank account details for tax and social contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT or social registrations are not automatically activated, file an ordinary application with the SIE or URSSAF and provide the RCS certificate to accelerate the assignment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the activity is classifiable as a digital marketing service (ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810); the local town hall (Mairie) is the relevant authority for any commercial operating licence to use the registered office in respect of planning rules.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating licence is required for app-store optimisation or SEO localization services; an ordinary permission d'exploitation commercial or a simple office lease declaration is sufficient.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Prefecture / Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) — France
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the service activity does not fall under Article R.122-2 of the French Environmental Code and requires no impact assessment or environmental permit.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No applicable emissions thresholds: the business generates no industrial wastewater, VOC/liquid discharges or hazardous waste. Any non-hazardous office waste must comply with the general sorting and disposal obligations under Articles L.541-1 et seq. of the Environmental Code.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The registered office must comply with French workplace safety regulations (Code du travail), including on-site access, installation, fire-safety provisions, electrical inspections, and ergonomic conditions; a simple declaration of occupancy and a certificate of compliance from the fire-safety inspector or the landlord is required for office premises. For service-only offices, no specific civil-defence permit is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP) under the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty. Digital portal: impots.gouv.fr for tax filing; formal entity and VAT registration via the official single window at guichet-entreprises.fr (operated by the Réseau des Chambres de Commerce et d'Industrie).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The non-resident shareholder establishes a French SAS by filing the incorporation dossier through guichet-entreprises.fr. Upon successful registration, the company automatically receives a SIREN number (9-digit INSEE identifier) and a SIRET establishment number. The French tax authority (DGFIP) then automatically assigns the intra-Community VAT number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire, format 'FR' + 2-digit control key + 11-digit SIREN). The VAT number can be verified and extracted via the French VAT number portal or the EU VIES system. No separate application form is required for a standard SAS, but for a non-resident-managed SAS the agent (président) must submit identity, registered office proof, and a declaration of beneficial ownership to the Companies Registry (RCS) as part of the dossier. If a French establishment (fixed base) is opened, a separate SIRET for that establishment is generated automatically; for a purely non-resident-managed SAS with no French fixed establishment, the single SIREN and VAT number suffice for tax compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SAS is treated as a French tax-resident corporation subject to corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS) on its worldwide profits. There is no pass-through or transparent election available under French domestic law; a French SAS cannot be treated as a partnership for French tax purposes. The standard IS headline rate is 25% (20% for small-business reduced rate is not applicable to the SAS default regime unless the entity meets the statutory SME thresholds, but the default classification remains Entity_Level_Taxation). The tax domicile of the SAS is in France (place of effective management is presumed to be the registered office unless proven otherwise). Territoriality: under domestic law, the SAS is taxed on French-source income and foreign income is potentially taxed subject to treaty relief; however, as a French incorporated entity it is fully resident and taxable on worldwide profits under the global taxation principle, with foreign tax credit relief under the relevant tax treaties. The reduced 15% IS rate for qualifying SMEs (up to €42,000 profit) is available only for companies satisfying independent SME criteria and is not part of the default classification; it is an elective/qualifying regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style 'check-the-box' election exists in France. The SAS cannot elect pass-through treatment. Available statutory elections for a French SAS include: (i) option for the tax-integrated regime (régime d'intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A of the French General Tax Code (CGI), allowing a parent SAS with at least 95% ownership to consolidate French subsidiaries' results, effective for a 5-year renewable term; (ii) election for VAT liability on rental real estate (option for VAT on let bare premises) under Article 260 CGI; (iii) option for the simplified VAT settlement scheme (régime simplifié) where the annual turnover threshold is met, electing semi-annual VAT payments instead of monthly; (iv) election to use the foreign tax credit (crédit d'impôt) or deduction method for foreign income under treaty provisions; (v) for hybrid mismatch purposes, France applies the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) rules under Articles 212 bis, 212 ter and 237 septies CGI, and any hybrid loan or branch instrument must be declared on the annual tax return (form 2758-SD for transfer pricing and hybrid documentation). A non-resident SAS parent may elect to be treated as a fiscal integration head if it has a French permanent establishment, which is subject to specific administrative approval; otherwise the SAS is taxed standalone.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée) — French Value Added Tax (VAT), governed by Articles 256 to 289 of the French General Tax Code (CGI), in conformity with EU VAT Directive (Council Directive 2006/112/EC).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 10,000 (annual EU-wide distance sales of goods or cross-border remote/digital B2C telecoms, broadcasting and electronic services threshold under Article 258 and 259 CGI and EU OSS regime). For the French SAS providing B2B services, there is NO registration threshold — the supplier must self-assess French VAT on the reverse charge basis when the B2B customer is French VAT-registered. For B2C digital/ASO/SEO localization services provided by the French SAS to non-VAT-registered customers located in the EU, the relevant threshold for applying the destination-country VAT via the OSS scheme remains EUR 10,000 (EU-wide cross-border supply); below this threshold, home-country (French) VAT applies to such EU B2C supplies. For domestic French B2C supplies, there is no registration threshold once the SAS performs any taxable transaction in France. For non-resident suppliers of ASO/SEO services into France, the B2C threshold is EUR 0 (no registration minimum), and the non-resident supplier must register for French VAT or use the non-union OSS scheme for electronic services where the global EU B2C revenue is below EUR 10,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has enacted a phased real-time e-invoicing mandate for all VAT-taxable persons established in France. The legal framework is set in Articles 1929 and 289 bis CGI and the 2024-2039 Finance Act implementation schedule. Developer timeline: (i) from 1 September 2026, all taxable persons established in France must be able to receive all invoices electronically in a structured format via the Public Invoicing Portal (Portail Public de Facturation, PPF) using an approved Dematerialisation Partner Platform (PDP) or a licensed operator; (ii) from 1 September 2026, large enterprises must issue e-invoices; (iii) from 1 September 2027, SMEs and micro-enterprises must issue e-invoices. Mandatory technical standards: structured electronic invoice format (Factur-X, UBL, CII) or the hybrid mixed format; transmission via the PPF with a mandatory unique identifier (Numéro d'identification de facturation) for each invoice; audit file (Fichier des Écritures Comptables, FEC) submission to DGFIP on request. Real-time transaction clearance (e-invoice clearances) is executed by the PPF/PDP platforms: each invoice must be transmitted with metadata (supplier VAT number, customer VAT number, transaction type, VAT amount, payment due date, and a cryptographic signature where required). No physical tax stamp or digital stamping is required; instead, the PPF performs automated cross-validation against the VAT return and EC Sales List. Non-compliance penalties: 5% per invoice of the total invoice amount (minimum EUR 15, maximum EUR 375 per invoice) plus a separate EUR 15 per transaction for data transmission failures; anti-fraud fine of up to EUR 1,500 for missing e-invoice data (EUR 7,500 for aggravating circumvention).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For the French SAS providing ASO/SEO localization services (ISIC 7310) to foreign customers, the applicable tax treatment is NOT an 'export zero-rating' but the extraterritoriality rule for B2B services under Article 259-1 CGI and Article 43 of the EU VAT Regulation 282/2011. Where the recipient is a taxable person (i.e. a VAT-registered business) established outside the EU or in another EU state, the supply of services is deemed to take place at the customer's place of establishment; consequently, the French SAS must NOT charge French VAT on the invoice, and the supply falls outside the scope of French VAT. This B2B rule has no formal threshold, and there is no requirement to obtain prior approval. For services where the foreign customer is a private individual / non-business consumer (B2C), the services are deemed supplied in France (because the supplier is established in France) and are therefore subject to French VAT at 20% unless the service is physically performed outside the EU (e.g. on-site SEO work in the USA may qualify for extraterritoriality under Article 259-2 CGI only if the service relates to immovable property located abroad or is physically performed abroad and enjoyed outside the EU). For goods exports (if the SAS ships promotional merchandise or physical localization kits), zero-rating applies under the legal export exemption of Article 262-1 CGI, which requires the goods to leave the EU within 90 days of supply. The B2B foreign customer VAT number must be validated via the VIES database for EU counterparties; for non-EU customers, a declaration of business status (attestation) is required. The service contract must have clear economic substance: no sham provision, no shell-company recipient, and the service must be genuinely consumed/benefited from outside France.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: For services (B2B): signed service contract specifying the customer's VAT identification number (VIES-validated for EU clients), the nature and scope of ASO/SEO localization deliverables, the place of performance and jurisdiction clauses; supplier invoice with the mention 'Exonération de TVA — Article 259-1 CGI — Client assujetti établi hors France' (or reverse-charge mention for EU B2B clients: 'TVA due par le preneur, article 283-1 CGI'); bank transfer or SWIFT payment record from the foreign customer's account evidencing actual cross-border remuneration; beneficial-ownership declaration of the foreign customer for non-EU entities (attestation from the customer); any supporting delivery evidence such as geo-IP server logs, ASO store listing screenshots showing the target country, and email/communication records from the foreign customer.

For goods exports (if merchandise is physically shipped out of the EU): customs export declaration (EX-Document / CAU — Carte Administrative Unique) with the export date and customs office stamp; Bill of Lading (B/L) or Airway Bill (AWB); proof of departure from the EU within 90 days; commercial invoice containing the export exemption mention under Article 262-1 CGI; inward remittance certificate (Certificat de rapatriement) from the bank acknowledging the foreign-sourced payment.

For B2C digital services supplied to non-EU private consumers: optional extraterritoriality declaration and the customer's non-EU address/IP-address evidence (geo-location logs of the App Store / Google Play user, national identity card or passport copy, IP-country log from the ASO campaign dashboard).
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The French tax administration (Direction Nationale d'Enquêtes Fiscales, DNE) and the National Customs and Indirect Taxation Office (Direction Nationale du Renseignement et des Enquêtes Douanières, DNRED) conduct targeted audits on agencies claiming B2B extraterritoriality for digital services. On audit, the taxpayer bears the burden of proving the customer's business status, the real economic substance of the cross-border supply, and the absence of a French taxable nexus. Absent adequate documentation, the supply is recharacterised as taxable in France, giving rise to: (i) retrospective clawback of the VAT not declared, plus late-payment interest (intérêts de retard) at 0.20% per month from the original due date; (ii) a 40% additional penalty for 'absence de bonne foi' (good-faith deficiency) under Article 1728 CGI, or 80% for 'manœuvres frauduleuses' or recharacterisation as an artificial arrangement under Article 1729-1 CGI; (iii) a further 5% penalty for failing to file the recapitulative statement (EC Sales List) or insufficient data under Article 1788 CGI; (iv) where hybrid mismatch or sham arrangements are detected (e.g. a shell company intermediary taking the income to avoid French VAT), the anti-abuse provision of Article 2325 CGI allows fiscal recharacterisation and joint and several liability for the intermediary; (v) criminal penalties for VAT fraud (Article 1741 CGI) can reach EUR 750,000 fines and 7 years' imprisonment where the under-declared VAT exceeds the criminal threshold and involves false documentation. Additionally, for goods exports, any mismatch between the customs declaration and the physical shipment or a false inward remittance certificate automatically triggers a full clawback of the zero-rated VAT and the application of the export forfeiture fine (amende forfaitaire) of up to 10% of the transaction value under Article 413 bis of the French Customs Code.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF) as the national monetary authority, exercising exchange-control reporting and balance-of-payments oversight under the Code Monétaire et Financier (CMF) in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB) and the European Systemic Risk Board. The Direction Générale du Trésor at the French Ministry of Economy administers financial sanctions policy, while the BdF Balance-of-Payments Directorate receives mandatory statistical declarations under EU Regulation 1849/2005, EU Regulation 2015/847 on transfers of funds, and the free-movement-of-capital framework of Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro has full de jure capital and current-account convertibility in France. No government exchange-control permit is required for cross-border payments, profit repatriation, dividend distributions, intercompany loans, or liquidation distributions to non-resident shareholders, save for transactions involving sanctioned jurisdictions or designated persons under EU/UN/OFAC lists. An SAS may freely pay dividends after annual-account approval; the standard dividend withholding tax is 25% for corporate shareholders (12.8% income tax plus 17.2% social levies for natural persons), reducible under tax treaties or eliminated at 0% for an eligible EU corporate shareholder holding at least 10% of the capital for two years (or a 24-month holding commitment) under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (2011/96/EU). The true residual constraints are tax anti-avoidance rules—interest and royalty payments must demonstrate economic substance to avoid recharacterization under Article 212 bis of the French General Tax Code, the EU ATAD interest-limitation rule (Article 212 quinquies), and DAC-6 cross-border arrangement disclosure—not currency convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France applies no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio for service export receipts in euros; the CMF imposes only declarative reporting, not repatriation or conversion. Any enterprise that executes cross-border settlements exceeding €750,000 in aggregate per calendar month must file a Banque de France balance-of-payments declaration (OPR e-declaration). For the ASO/SEO localization agency, export proceeds are services invoiced to non-resident clients classified under BOP service purpose codes 204 (advertising and market research) or 211 (telecommunications, computer, and information services). Failure to file triggers penalties of between €1,500 and €3,000 per omission plus interest under CMF R. 165-1 et seq. Proceeds may remain in the EUR treasury account, be converted at market rates, or be applied to operational disbursements without prior approval.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Compte Courant) with optional segregated sub-account for client-fund escrow
Operational multi-currency account (Compte Courant en devises) with integrated treasury desk
Operational Account for local-region substance building and short-term cash management

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE S.A. — Banque Populaire Rives de Paris / Natixis
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with client-fund escrow (Compte de dépôt de fonds clients) capability

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: HSBC Continental Europe S.A. (now CCF S.A.)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: International operational account with multi-currency cross-border rails

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: HIGH for the target payment rails. Wise Europe SA (licensed as an Electronic Money Institution by the National Bank of Belgium, passported into France under PSD2) and Payoneer Financial Services Ireland Ltd (EMI licensed by the Central Bank of Ireland, passported into France) may lawfully open remote corporate accounts and execute cross-border payments on behalf of the SAS. Under CMF Articles L. 525-1 to L. 525-3, EMIs may not take deposits or grant commercial credit; client funds must be safeguarded (segregated) with a credit institution. Offshore (non-EU) EMIs without an EU-licensed establishment—such as a UK-only EMI after Brexit—have no direct French passport and may not hold the SAS's treasury balances; the SAS must therefore channel the bulk of its liquidity through an EU-passported EMI or a tier-1 French bank. The SAS should maintain a tier-1 bank account as the bank-relationship anchor for substance, credit references, and potential financing, while using Wise_B2B and Payoneer as cost-effective receiving and vendor-disbursement rails for non-resident clients and independent contractors.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For the first tier-1 French bank account, at least one director with signature authority (the SAS Président or a mandataire) must in practice appear physically at a French branch, unless the bank applies the compliant video-KYC path under CMF Article L. 561-5, which requires notarized and apostilled corporate documents, certified passports, and a proof-of-address document dated within the last three months. A non-resident director may delegate signature rights to a French-resident manager via a formal corporate resolution and notarized power of attorney, but the fifth EU AML Directive beneficial-ownership rules remain strictly applied. Remote opening without any French physical contact is ordinarily unavailable at BNP Paribas and Société Générale for a new company with no historical relationship; the fintech EMIs (Wise, Payoneer) permit fully remote opening within 3–10 business days via video-identity verification, an extract of the Registre du Commerce (Kbis), board resolutions, and UBO declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) not fiscally domiciled in France
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled passport or national ID; certified residential address proof (utility bill or lease dated within 90 days); a source-of-wealth statement backed by account/brokerage statements and property deeds; a French or foreign tax-residency certificate; and a CRS self-certification file (French forms 5000/5024) listing every jurisdiction of tax residence for each natural-person UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital marketing and SEO/ASO business model perceived as opaque because traffic sources and payment flows are intangible
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed client service agreements; itemized invoices reconciling treasury inflows to deliverables (App Store/Google Play dashboards, keyword-ranking records, localization files); evidence of a legitimate app-development portfolio; historical bank statements showing a coherent payment trail; a written AML-compliant business-narrative statement confirming no click-farm, ad-fraud, or synthetic-traffic monetization; and audited annual accounts or an Expert-Comptable attestation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Name-screen hits on entity, board members, or shareholders against sanctions/PEP watches
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport and residence-permit copies; name-change or marriage certificates to eliminate false-positive homonyms; a sanctions-screening clearance letter from the onboarding bank; a beneficial-ownership attestation evidencing no Russian, Belarusian, Iranian, Syrian, North Korean, or Crimean nexus; and an internal client-acceptance policy requiring enhanced senior-management review for any counterparty in FATF high-risk jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Treasury routing that appears artificially fintech-concentrated (frequent sweeps from Wise or Payoneer to an offshore account)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury policy; executed FX-hedging policy; documented, signed invoices underlying each EUR/USD/GBP conversion; a tax representation letter from the French Expert-Comptable confirming no fabricated transfer pricing; and an organizational chart evidencing the SAS as the operating and income-apportioning entity rather than a pass-through intermediary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment volumes crossing the €750,000/month Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting threshold
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Filed OPR/BOP declaration receipts with timestamp; a complete intercompany reconciliation workbook; board minutes approving treasury movements; and the underlying contractual documentation demonstrating the commercial purpose of each reported flow.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: A French SAS has no minimum capital requirement, so a capital injection may be routed by SEPA Credit Transfer (from EU shareholders) or SWIFT MT103 (from non-EU shareholders) into the SAS operational account. The wire must include: the beneficiary legal name exactly as on the Kbis extract, the SAS RCS number, full UBO identification, the Banque de France balance-of-payments purpose code for direct investment ('Prise de participation au capital' for equity contributions or 'Prêts interentreprises' for shareholder current-account advances), and the invoice/capital-resolution reference. The shareholder must provide the bank with its source-of-funds pack—bank statement, signed capital-increase resolution, and a source-of-wealth declaration. For in-kind contributions exceeding €7,500 or representing more than half of the share capital, a Commissaire aux Apports valuation report is mandatory. The SAS must file the capital-increase form (M2) at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce within one month of receipt. A monthly or annual balance-of-payments declaration is due wherever the combined cross-border movements exceed the €750,000 threshold.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The core clearing rail for an ASO/SEO localization agency is SWIFT MT103 for non-EU vendor payments (subtitle translation studios, performance-budget ad spends on Meta/Google, independent localization linguists) and SEPA Credit Transfer / SEPA Instant for intra-EU or French vendor disbursements. For large recurring deliveries (≥ €500,000), a Commercial Letter of Credit governed by UCP 600 may be opened through the tier-1 bank with a deferred payment clause; however, services businesses predominantly operate open account using MT103 with a parent-company guarantee or a conditional performance bank bond. Mandatory French transfer purpose codes are attached to each outbound payment: 204 (advertising and market research), 211 (telecommunications, computer, and information services), 291 (management consultancy), and 110 (goods for resale). The SAS must also comply with the French e-invoicing reform (Ordinance 2021-1054) and apply reverse-charge VAT treatment to non-resident vendor invoices in order to recover input VAT credits. Payments to FATF-listed or sanctioned jurisdictions must be automatically blocked or escalated to the compliance officer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF, EUR/JPY) with tenors up to 24 months, executed under an ISDA or FBF (Fédération Bancaire Française) master agreement with a Eurozone credit institution or MiFID-licensed investment firm; the OTC derivative is subject to EMIR clearing-determination, collateral, and trade-repository reporting obligations.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on INR, IDR, BRL, KRW, TRY, NGN, and other restricted-convertibility currencies, used to hedge contractor payments in emerging markets; permitted when executed by a MiFID-licensed broker and settled only through a EUR cash difference.

Cross-Currency Swaps (XCCY) and Plain Vanilla FX Options (EUR Put / USD Call, EUR Put / GBP Call) for hedging the net investment in a foreign subsidiary or the refinancing of a strategic acquisition; post-trade documentation must be segregated under EMIR and CMF Article L. 533-1, and speculative or uncovered option positions are outside the permitted treasury policy.

Multi-currency conversion wallets of Wise_B2B and Payoneer, which execute spot exchange at a published mid-market-derived rate under the EMI's currency-exchange service authorization (CMF Article L. 315-1); these are permissible treasury arrangements but cannot be marketed as deposit-taking or interest-bearing products under PSD2 fee-transparency rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry (Greffe du tribunal de commerce), generally through the INPI one-stop portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must generally be approved within six months after financial year-end and filed within one month after approval, or within two months after approval when filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may result in a court injunction and a civil fine generally up to EUR 1,500, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance. Administrative strike-off is not automatic solely because accounts are late; it may follow separate registry action after formal notice where statutory conditions are met.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Form 2065 with supporting schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Service des impôts des entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by the second business day after 1 May for a calendar-year taxpayer, with an additional electronic filing period normally available; for a non-calendar year, within three months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, potentially increased to 40% for deliberate failure or 80% for fraudulent conduct, plus late-payment interest and applicable tax assessments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business tax compliance and payment, including Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Tax payment is generally due by 15 December annually. Annual filing is required only where a specific declaration, exemption claim, change, or tax-base update applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment generally attracts a 5% surcharge and late-payment interest. Non-filing of a required declaration may trigger assessment by the administration and penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI beneficial ownership register through the French one-stop portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No routine annual filing where information remains unchanged. Changes must generally be reported within 30 days after the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or maintain accurate beneficial ownership information may lead to formal notice, criminal penalties for responsible persons, and restrictions or registry action against the entity.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory for an SAS meeting at least two of three thresholds at financial year-end: balance sheet total exceeding EUR 5 million, annual turnover excluding tax exceeding EUR 10 million, and average workforce exceeding 50 employees. Additional appointment rules may apply to certain groups and controlled or controlling entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the French Accounting Standards Authority (ANC) regulations. IFRS may be used in limited circumstances but is not the default statutory framework for an SAS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a standalone annual beneficial ownership confirmation where the recorded information remains unchanged. The SAS must maintain accurate beneficial ownership data and report every change in ownership, control, or identifying information generally within 30 days. Share transfers must be documented in the share transfer register and reflected in the register of shareholders.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders and share transfers
Register of beneficial owners or accessible beneficial ownership records
Register of decisions of the president and other corporate bodies where applicable
Minute books and executed corporate resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 300-1,500 per year, depending on location, mail handling, and administrative services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,000-8,000 per year for a small or medium SAS requiring a statutory auditor; no statutory audit fee applies if appointment is not legally required

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% corporate income tax rate on the first EUR 38,120 of annual taxable profit for eligible SMEs with turnover below EUR 10 million; 95% participation exemption on qualifying dividends under the French parent-subsidiary regime; research tax credit (CIR) at 30% up to EUR 100 million of eligible R&D expenditure; innovation tax credit (CII) at 20% for qualifying SME innovation expenditure; no sector-specific tax holiday applies to app growth/ASO/SEO localization agencies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire n° 2065 – Déclaration de résultats; filed electronically via the EDI-TDFC service on impots.gouv.fr (TéléTVA portal).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly prepayment instalments paid on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December; final balance paid with the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the annual corporate income tax return must be filed no later than the second business day following 1 May of the following year. For an off-calendar fiscal year, the return must be filed within three months of the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form of the SAS, company name, registered head office address, SIREN/SIRET number, APE/NAF code 7310Z, opening and closing dates of the fiscal year, and principal business activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French SAS files as a French tax resident. Use the French registered address and SIREN. Non-resident shareholders are not joint filers; their tax residence and shareholding percentages are recorded in the share register and shareholders' resolutions, not on the French corporate return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre B – Bénéfice net / Déficit (Box B)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit or tax loss in euros after accounting adjustments, including deduction of allowable expenses and add-back of non-deductible items such as excessive management fees and non-deductible VAT penalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the worldwide taxable profit of the French entity. Do not include the foreign personal income or foreign corporate profits of non-resident shareholders. Any intercompany charges to non-resident affiliates must be arm's-length and documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre C – Capitaux propres / Affectation du résultat (Box C)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Share capital, legal reserves, retained earnings, current-year profit or loss, and proposed profit appropriation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure declared profit appropriation matches the formal shareholders' decisions. If dividends are distributed to a non-resident shareholder, the minutes and dividend voucher must identify the shareholder's name, tax residence and tax identification number for withholding tax purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre F – Crédits d'impôts / Retenues à la source (Box F)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits such as CIR/CII, foreign tax credits, French withholding taxes already suffered, and any imputed source taxes to be offset against corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot claim French CIR/CII or personal foreign tax credits on the SAS corporate return. The French company claims only credits legally belonging to the entity; non-resident dividend recipients must seek treaty relief separately.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic 10% increase of the tax due if the return is not submitted within 30 days after formal notice; deliberate misstatement attracts a 40% penalty; abusive sham arrangement attracts an 80% penalty. Monthly late-payment interest accrues at 0.20% of the unpaid tax. Persistent non-filing permits enforced recovery through avis de mise en recouvrement and additional criminal exposure under article 1742 CGI.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on gross dividends distributed by a French SAS to a non-resident corporate shareholder (article 119 bis 2 CGI), subject to tax treaty reduction and EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced treaty rate at source, the non-resident shareholder must submit to the French paying company a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign competent authority before the payment date, together with a statement of beneficial ownership and, where applicable, evidence of the minimum shareholding period required by the applicable double tax agreement or EU Directive. The French paying company must retain the TRC in its tax file. If treaty relief is not applied at source, the non-resident may file a refund claim with DGFiP through the French tax procedure (réclamation contentieuse), attaching the TRC and full dividend documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-resident companies are subject to a statutory French withholding tax of 25% on gross income; the EU Interest-Royalties Directive may reduce this to 0% for associated companies of EU Member States, and many tax treaties provide for 5% or 10%. Interest paid to non-resident creditors is generally subject to limited French withholding tax, principally 25% on certain debt instruments not covered by the bank-credit exemption; EU Directive and tax treaties commonly reduce the rate to 0% for arm's-length interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 of consolidated annual turnover or total balance-sheet assets. A French entity or group exceeding this threshold must maintain Master File and Local File documentation. A French ultimate parent of an MNEs group with consolidated revenue above EUR 750,000,000 must file a country-by-country report (form 2258-SD). Below these thresholds, mandatory documentation is not triggered, but the taxpayer must still demonstrate arm's-length pricing upon audit.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a separate Economic Substance Regulation filing regime comparable to low-tax jurisdictions. Nevertheless, economic substance is tested through the general anti-abuse doctrine (abus de droit), controlled-foreign-company rules, anti-treaty-shopping provisions, and the OECD BEPS tests. A French SAS acting as an ASO/SEO localization agency must have real staff, premises, contracts, decision-making and profit-allocating functions. A shell structure with no genuine operational substance in France risks reclassification, loss of treaty benefits, and 80% fraud penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully concealing turnover from ASO/SEO localization services by omitting invoices from French accounting records, using foreign payment rails such as Wise B2B or Payoneer to divert payments, and suppressing cash receipts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years under article 1741 CGI; aggravated fraud involving concealment of tax base may raise the fine to EUR 3,000,000 and imprisonment to 7 years; civil tax adjustment carries a 40% bad-faith penalty plus 0.20% monthly late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president and director-generals may be criminally prosecuted personally. Through article L.651-2 of the French Commercial Code, directors may be ordered to cover corporate tax debts for mismanagement. Travel bans, asset freezing, and confiscation of personal assets may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-Filing or Materially False Tax Returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file Form 2065 by the statutory deadline or filing accounting annexes that materially misstate revenue, headcount, or intercompany transactions after formal notice.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Automatic 10% late-filing increase; 40% penalty for deliberate inaccuracy; 80% penalty for fraudulent manoeuvre; late-payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month; failure to comply with repeated notices may trigger enforced tax collection and additional fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or knowingly approve false declarations may be personally liable for penalties and interest, subject to criminal sanctions under articles 1742 and 1743 CGI, including imprisonment and fines; civil liability may cover the entire tax shortfall.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Billing related non-resident affiliates for ASO/SEO localization services at prices departing from arm's-length value, or shifting French profits through excessive management fees, marketing commissions, intangibles licensing, or cost allocations without local substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGFiP may re-determine French taxable income at arm's-length level and impose additional corporate income tax plus 0.20% monthly interest; deliberate mispricing attracts a 40% penalty; artificial avoidance arrangements attract an 80% penalty under article 1729 CG.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who initiate or approve fictitious pricing arrangements may be held personally liable under civil mismanagement rules; where the arrangement is fraudulent, criminal tax evasion charges and disqualification from management may follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a French SAS with no real local employees, premises, business activity, or decisions while holding client contracts, ownership of app growth intangibles, or cash flows for the purpose of obtaining treaty benefits, tax deferral or non-resident ownership advantages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The arrangement may be disregarded as an abuse of law under article L.64 of the French Tax Procedures Book; French tax is re-established against the true beneficial owner; the 80% abuse penalty is applied in addition to interest; treaty protections may be revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and beneficial owners may be jointly and severally liable for corporate tax and penalties; courts may prohibit the directors from managing a commercial enterprise and impose travel restrictions in criminal abuse cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register or update the beneficial owner details in the French Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), or refusing to identify the natural persons ultimately owning the SAS while receiving cross-border B2B payments through alternative payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Non-compliance with RBE disclosure carries criminal penalties, including fines up to EUR 15,000 and imprisonment of up to 6 months; separate anti-money-laundering breaches may result in account freezing, financial penalties by the ACPR, and transaction blockage by PSP providers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners are personally exposed to criminal fines and imprisonment; concealment of substantial beneficial ownership may lead to piercing of the corporate veil and personal seizure of bank accounts and assets where the company is used as a laundering vehicle.
